mainTopic: The סוטה's barley offering, and how the cup, water and dust for the bitter waters are prepared
overview: The amud finishes explaining why the סוטה's מנחה is barley, which is animal food. רבי מאיר says it is because she fed her lover fine foods. רבן גמליאל objects that this does not fit a poor woman, and says instead that she acted like an animal. A new משנה then describes the earthenware cup, the amount of water (חצי לוג, or a רביעית according to רבי יהודה), and the dust taken from under a marble tile in the היכל. In the גמרא, רבי ישמעאל requires a new cup, learning it from the מצורע through the shared word 'כלי'. The גמרא defends that comparison, and רבא adds that a blackened vessel is unfit. רבא then asks about a vessel that was whitened again, and the attempted proof is pushed away. Next, the גמרא explains why the כהן turns right and brings two ברייתות on where the dust must come from. The amud ends as אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה begins a teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason for the barley offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבן גמליאל spoke up because he heard רבי מאיר's reason: the סוטה fed her lover fine foods, so her offering is animal food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he heard רבי מאיר saying: She fed him the finest foods of the world, so her offering is animal food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what made רבן גמליאל speak up: he heard רבי מאיר give a reason for the barley offering, and he wanted to respond to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה's מנחה is barley, which people normally feed to animals. רבי מאיר links this to her sin: she spoiled her lover with fancy food, so her punishment is to bring plain animal food. It is a measure-for-measure reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the finest delicacies of the world

phrases.english: Because he heard Rabbi Meir saying:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן גמליאל; this is why he spoke up just before.

phrases.english: She fed him the delicacies of the world —
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man she secluded herself with.

phrases.english: therefore her offering is animal food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about the reason for the barley מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the barley offering repays her for feeding her lover delicacies.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: what about a poor woman?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי מאיר: his reason fits a rich woman, but a poor woman never had delicacies to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That works for a rich woman. But for a poor woman, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל attacks רבי מאיר's reason by showing a case where it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every סוטה brings barley, rich or poor. A poor woman could not afford fancy food for her lover, so 'she fed him delicacies' cannot be the reason for her barley. A reason that only fits some women cannot explain a law that applies to all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: that works out well (for this case)

phrases.english: He said to him: That works well for a rich woman,
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל is answering רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: but for a poor woman, what is there to say!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח עֲשִׁירָה, עֲנִיָּה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reason that the barley repays her for feeding her lover delicacies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The law applies to every סוטה, but the reason only fits a rich one. A poor סוטה could not have given delicacies.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's own reason: she acted like an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל gives a reason that fits every סוטה: since she behaved like an animal, her offering is animal food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: just as her actions were the actions of an animal, so too her offering is animal food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל replaces רבי מאיר's reason with a new one that works for rich and poor alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason is about her behavior, not her money. Any woman, rich or poor, who acted without restraint like an animal fits this reason. So it explains why every סוטה brings barley.
steps.whatToRemember: The barley offering is explained by her animal-like behavior, a reason that fits every סוטה. רבי מאיר's 'delicacies' reason was set aside because it fails for a poor woman.

phrases.english: Rather: just as her actions were the actions of an animal —
so too her offering is animal food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a replacement reason after the challenge in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The barley מנחה matches her animal-like conduct, which applies to every סוטה.

steps.title: The earthenware cup and half a log of water
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says the כהן brought an earthenware cup and poured into it half a לוג of water from the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The כהן would bring an earthenware cup and put into it half a לוג of water from the basin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and describes the first step in preparing the bitter waters: the cup and the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cup must be earthenware, and the water comes from the כיור, the washing basin in the מקדש. This is the opening, unnamed opinion: the amount is חצי לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (the start of a new משנה)
the copper washing basin in the מקדש

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה מֵבִיא פְּיָלִי שֶׁל חֶרֶס
phrases.english: MISHNAH: He would bring an earthenware cup
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן doing the סוטה procedure.

phrases.english: and he would put into it half a log
of water from the basin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה מֵבִיא פְּיָלִי שֶׁל חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water is half a לוג from the כיור, in an earthenware cup.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a quarter-log
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says only a רביעית of water is used, matching his view that less is written on the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a quarter of a לוג. Just as he reduces the writing, so he reduces the water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the amount of water. The משנה explains his view by tying it to his other opinion about the writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The writing on the scroll gets erased into the water. רבי יהודה holds that less text is written on the scroll, so less water is needed to erase it. His two opinions fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: the writing on the סוטה's scroll

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: a quarter.
phrases.notes: He means a quarter of a לוג, half of what the first opinion said.

phrases.english: Just as he reduces the writing,
so he reduces the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the amount of water in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a רביעית of water, since less writing needs less water to erase it.

steps.title: Taking dust from under the marble tile
steps.stepSummary: The כהן enters the היכל, turns right, lifts a marble tile by its ring, takes dust from beneath it, and puts enough into the water to be visible.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would enter the היכל and turn right. There was a spot there, an אמה by an אמה, with a marble tile that had a ring fixed in it to lift it. He would take dust from under it and put in enough so it could be seen on the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the next step: where the dust comes from and how much of it goes into the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dust had to come from the floor of the holy place, so a special marble tile with a ring was set up to reach the earth beneath. Only enough dust to be seen on the water is needed, not a set measure.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sanctuary building in the מקדש
one אמה by one אמה (a square about the size of a forearm on each side)

phrases.english: He would enter the Sanctuary and turn to his right,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָקוֹם הָיָה שָׁם אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה,
phrases.english: and there was a place there, a cubit by a cubit,
and a marble tablet,
and a ring was fixed in it
for when he lifts it,
and he takes dust from underneath it,
and he puts in enough that it will be visible on the water,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the procedure after the water is placed in the cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dust is taken from beneath a marble tile in the היכל, enough to be seen on the water.

steps.title: The verse behind the dust
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings the פסוק that commands taking dust from the floor of the משכן and putting it into the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And from the dust that is on the floor of the משכן, the כהן shall take and put it into the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up the dust procedure with its source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the dust must come from the floor of the משכן. That is why the כהן goes into the היכל and takes dust from under the floor tile, instead of using ordinary dirt from anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: as it is stated: “And from the dust that will be
on the floor of the Tabernacle, the priest shall take
and put it into the water.”
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:17

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּמִן הֶעָפָר אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בְּקַרְקַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the procedure described in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the dust is taken from the floor of the holy place and put into the water.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the cup must be new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל says the earthenware cup must be new.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: a new earthenware cup. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by adding a detail the משנה left out: according to רבי ישמעאל, the cup must be brand new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'an earthenware cup.' The ברייתא adds that רבי ישמעאל requires a new one. This sets up the next question about why.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
a new earthenware cup,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: פְּיָלִי שֶׁל חֶרֶס חֲדָשָׁה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the cup mentioned in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, the earthenware cup must be new.

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל requires a new cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי ישמעאל's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק by סוטה only says 'an earthenware vessel' and does not say 'new.' So the גמרא wants to know where the word 'new' comes from.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי ישמעאל learns that the cup must be new.

steps.title: Learning 'vessel' from the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from the word 'כלי' found both by סוטה and by מצורע: the מצורע's vessel must be new earthenware, so the סוטה's must be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'vessel' and 'vessel' from מצורע: just as there it is new earthenware, so here it is new earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל uses a גזירה שוה, a link between two places in the תורה that use the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the סוטה and the מצורע purification use an earthen 'כלי' with water. By the מצורע a new earthenware vessel is required. The shared word 'כלי' carries that requirement over to the סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: he learns (here, through a גזירה שוה)
just as there, so too here

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל requires a new cup for the סוטה by linking the word 'כלי' here to 'כלי' by the מצורע, where a new earthenware vessel is required.

phrases.english: He learns “vessel” “vessel” from the leper:
phrases.notes: The word 'כלי' shows up for the סוטה (במדבר 5:17) and for the מצורע (ויקרא 14:5), so one teaches about the other.

phrases.english: just as there it is new earthenware —
so too here it is new earthenware.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word 'כלי' by מצורע, where the vessel must be new earthenware.

steps.title: How do we know the מצורע's vessel must be new?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the מצורע's earthenware vessel must be new.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by the מצורע, how do we know the vessel must be new?
steps.whatsHappening: The whole comparison in Step 10 rests on the מצורע's vessel being new. The גמרא asks how we know that, and the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה learns from the מצורע, so the rule by the מצורע needs its own source. Without it, there is nothing for the סוטה to borrow.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the other case, here the מצורע)

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "There" means the מצורע from Step 10, whose vessel must be new earthenware.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule about the מצורע that Step 10 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the מצורע's earthenware vessel must be new.

steps.title: The vessel is compared to the fresh water next to it
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts the vessel together with מים חיים. Just as that water was never used for work, the vessel must also never have been used.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he shall slaughter one of the birds into an earthenware vessel over מים חיים.' Just as the מים חיים were never used for work, so too the vessel must never have been used for work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 11 from a פסוק about the מצורע's birds. It compares the vessel to the water mentioned right beside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מים חיים is fresh, flowing water that has never been used. Because the vessel appears in the same phrase, it takes on the same quality and must also be unused, meaning new.

keyTerms.meaning: Work; here, being used for something

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he shall slaughter the one bird
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:5

phrases.aramaic: אֶל כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ עַל מַיִם חַיִּים״,
phrases.english: into an earthenware vessel over living water."
Just as the "living water"
has had no work done with it,
so too the "vessel"
must have had no work done with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11's question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The vessel is compared to the unused מים חיים in the same פסוק, so the vessel must be unused (new).

steps.title: Then the סוטה should also need fresh spring water
steps.stepSummary: If the סוטה learns from the מצורע, the גמרא asks why she should not also need מים חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there the מצורע needs living water, so too here the סוטה should need living water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison one step further. If the סוטה borrows the 'new vessel' rule from the מצורע, she should also borrow the 'living water' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison works through the word 'כלי', and the מצורע's כלי comes together with מים חיים. So the challenge is that the comparison should bring the water requirement along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (the case we are learning about)

phrases.english: If so: just as there it is living water,
phrases.notes: "There" is the מצורע and "here" is the סוטה.

phrases.english: so too here it should be living water?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן מַיִם חַיִּים אַף כָּאן מַיִם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the comparison from Steps 10 and 12 to argue for a further requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the סוטה to the מצורע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison brings over the new vessel, it should also bring over the living water.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל agrees: spring water is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that according to רבי ישמעאל, the סוטה's water really must be spring water.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי ישמעאל, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not reject Step 13's idea. It says רבי ישמעאל really does hold that spring water is needed, and the next step brings proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'yes, that's right' answer. The question in Step 13 is not a problem for רבי ישמעאל, because he accepts that requirement too.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yishmael, it is indeed so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the conclusion of Step 13's challenge for רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Requiring spring water seemed like an unwanted result of the comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל really does require spring water.

steps.title: Proof: רבי ישמעאל requires spring water for the כיור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי ישמעאל says the water of the כיור must be spring water, while the חכמים allow any water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: about the water of the כיור, רבי ישמעאל says it is spring water, and the חכמים say it may be from any other water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves Step 14's claim by bringing a dispute about the water of the כיור, the washing basin in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the סוטה's water is taken from the כיור. So if רבי ישמעאל requires the כיור to hold spring water, the סוטה's water is spring water too. The חכמים disagree and allow any water.

keyTerms.meaning: The washing basin in the מקדש

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
The water of the basin, Rabbi Yishmael says:
It is spring water,
and the Rabbis say: it may be from other waters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives proof for the claim in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל requires spring water for the סוטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's report of the dispute about the water of the כיור.

steps.title: The comparison can be broken: the מצורע has extra requirements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges learning the סוטה from the מצורע, because the מצורע needs cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about the מצורע? He is special, since he requires cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the whole comparison from Step 10. It says the מצורע is a stricter case, so we may not be able to learn the סוטה from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע's purification needs extra items, עץ ארז, אזוב and שני תולעת, which the סוטה does not need. Since the מצורע has extra requirements, perhaps the new-vessel rule is one of them and does not carry over to the סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted; the comparison can be broken

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule about the סוטה. The גמרא is only questioning whether we are allowed to learn the סוטה from the מצורע at all.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about the leper? He is special, because he requires
cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of the comparison to challenging whether the comparison works at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's comparison of the סוטה to the מצורע through the word 'כלי' (Step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצורע has special requirements the סוטה does not, so his rules may not carry over to her.

steps.title: רבה: The verse points to the vessel already mentioned
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the words 'in an earthen vessel' point back to a vessel the תורה already spoke about, the vessel of the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The verse says 'in an earthen vessel.' This means the vessel I already told you about.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge from Step 16. He shows that the verse itself ties the סוטה to the מצורע, but only for the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says 'the earthen vessel' for the סוטה as if we already know which vessel it means. That points back to the earthen vessel of the מצורע. So the link between them is about the vessel only, not about עץ ארז, אזוב and שני תולעת.

keyTerms.meaning: That I already told you about

phrases.english: Rabba said: The verse states:
"In an earthen vessel"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:17

phrases.english: a vessel that I have already told you about.
phrases.notes: He means the earthen vessel used for the מצורע, which the תורה described earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה, אָמַר קְרָא: בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about learning the סוטה from the מצורע by showing the verse links only the vessel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the סוטה learns from the מצורע, she should need everything the מצורע needs, including cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse links them only through the vessel, which it calls 'the vessel I already told you about.'

steps.title: רבא: A vessel with a blackened surface is unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the vessel is fit only if its outside has not turned black, because the vessel must be unchanged like the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: They taught this only when the outside of the vessel was not blackened. But if its outside was blackened, it is unfit. Why? It is like the water. Just as the water must be unchanged, so too the vessel must be unchanged.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new limit to the rule about the vessel. A vessel whose outside has turned black from use cannot be used for the סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse puts the vessel together with the water. Since the water must be unchanged, the vessel must also look unchanged. A blackened vessel has changed, so it is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case where...

phrases.english: Rava says: They only taught
when its surface was not blackened,
phrases.notes: Literally 'its face,' meaning the outside of the vessel.

phrases.english: but if its surface was blackened, they are unfit.
What is the reason? It is similar to water:
just as the water is unchanged,
so too the vessel must be unchanged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נִתְאַכְּמוּ פָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new condition for the vessel, using the same comparison to water used earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel whose outside has blackened is unfit for the סוטה, because the vessel must be unchanged like the water.

steps.title: רבא asks: What if the blackened vessel is whitened again?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a blackened vessel that was put back into the furnace and turned white again becomes fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If the vessels became blackened, and he put them back into the furnace and they turned white, what is the law? Do we say that once they were disqualified, they stay disqualified? Or perhaps since they went back to how they were, they are fit again?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on his own ruling and asks a real question. The next step will try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. Maybe once something became unfit, it stays unfit forever. Or maybe since it looks unchanged again, it is fit again.

keyTerms.meaning: Once pushed aside (made unfit), it stays pushed aside
Since it went back, it went back (to being fit)

phrases.english: Rava asked: If they became blackened
and he put them back into the furnace
and they turned white, what is the law?
Do we say: once they were pushed aside, they stay pushed aside,
or perhaps since they went back, they went back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a follow-up case to רבא's own ruling about a blackened vessel.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vessel that became unfit by blackening becomes fit again once it is whitened in the furnace.

steps.title: Proof from the מצורע's items tied to a basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's ruling that the מצורע's items used to tie a basket stay unfit, even though they can be straightened out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר says: Cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool that he used to tie his basket behind him are unfit. But there they can be straightened out again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבא's question with a case about the מצורע. It shows that items can stay unfit even after they are restored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items used to tie a basket can be smoothed out so they look unused again. Still, רבי אלעזר says they are unfit. The גמרא wants to learn from this that once something is disqualified, it stays disqualified. The next step challenges that.

keyTerms.meaning: Cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool, used to purify the מצורע
They can go back and be straightened out

steps.whatToRemember: רבא rules that a blackened vessel is unfit. The גמרא tries to settle his follow-up question with the מצורע's items, but the next step pushes the proof away, so the question about a re-whitened vessel stays unsettled here.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Elazar says:
Cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool
with which he tied his basket behind him are unfit.
But there they can be straightened out again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבא's question from Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That something disqualified stays disqualified even if it is later restored (כיון דאידחו אידחו).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling that the מצורע's cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool used to tie a basket are unfit, even though they can be straightened out again.

steps.title: The basket case is different because the items were damaged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the מצורע's items. Those items stay unfit because tying them scraped them, so they never truly return to how they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the items are different because they were peeled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof brought in the last step. The basket case cannot teach us about the vessel that turned white again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying the cedar wood, hyssop and wool into a basket scrapes them, and straightening them does not undo that damage. The vessel that went back into the furnace may truly return to its first state, so the two cases are not alike. רבא's question about the vessel stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other case
They were really peeled or scraped

steps.confusionAlert: This does not answer רבא's question either way. It only shows that the proof does not work, so the question about the re-whitened vessel is left unresolved here.

phrases.english: There, it is because they were peeled.
phrases.notes: Tying the items into a basket scraped them, so they can never truly go back to how they looked before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the basket items and the re-whitened vessel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The basket items were physically damaged by peeling, so they cannot be compared to a vessel that may fully return to its original state

steps.title: Why does the כהן turn to the right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the כהן enters the היכל and turns right, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: He entered the היכל and turned to his right, and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks why the כהן turns specifically to the right. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the כהן going into the היכל to take dust for the סוטה's water. It says he turns right but does not say why. The גמרא wants the source for this detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He entered the Sanctuary and turned to his right, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. The כהן is going in to get the dust.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כהן turns to the right when entering the היכל

steps.title: All turns should be to the right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a general rule: every turn you make should be to the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: All turns that you turn should be only to the right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning right here is not a special rule for the סוטה. It is one example of a wider rule that whenever you turn, you turn toward the right.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
All turns that you turn
should be only toward the right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A general rule that all turns should be made to the right

steps.title: Could the dust be prepared outside and brought in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the place in the floor, then brings a ברייתא. The ברייתא first suggests that, from the words 'of the dust that is', the כהן might prepare dust outside and bring it in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: There was a place there, an אמה, and so on. The חכמים taught: 'And of the dust that is'. One might think he could prepare it outside and bring it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about the dust step by step. This step raises a first possible mistake, which the next step will correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only said 'of the dust that is', any dust might do, even dust from outside the היכל. The ברייתא raises this idea so it can show which words in the פסוק rule it out.

phrases.english: There was a place there, a cubit, etc.
phrases.notes: Another quote from the משנה: a cubit-wide spot in the floor with a marble tile covering loose dust.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And of the dust that is",
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:17

phrases.english: one might think he could prepare it outside and bring it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברייתא begins a reading of the פסוק by suggesting that dust could be brought in from outside

steps.title: The dust must be from the floor of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק says 'on the floor of the משכן', so the dust must come from inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'On the floor of the משכן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea of bringing dust from outside by pointing to more words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on the floor of the משכן' tie the dust to the floor of the holy building itself. So dust prepared outside is not fit.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "On the floor of the Tabernacle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion in Step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dust must come from the floor of the משכן itself

steps.title: Could he dig up the floor with axes?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a new possible mistake: if the dust must be from the floor, maybe he may dig it out with axes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it says 'on the floor of the משכן', one might think he may dig with axes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a second possible mistake that comes from the answer just given. The next step will rule it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the dust must be from the floor, one might think any way of getting it is allowed, even breaking up the floor. The ברייתא raises this to show that another word in the פסוק blocks it.

phrases.english: If only "on the floor of the Tabernacle",
one might think he may dig with axes —

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּקַרְקַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן, יָכוֹל יַחְפּוֹר בְּקַרְדּוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new possible mistake that comes from the answer in Step 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the כהן may dig into the floor to get the dust

steps.title: The dust must already be there
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words 'that is': the dust must already be lying there loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'that is'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא blocks the idea of digging by pointing to the words 'that is' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The dust that is' means dust that is already there and loose. Dust you have to chop out of the floor does not fit these words.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "that is."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion in Step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dust must already be lying loose on the floor, so digging is not allowed

steps.title: If loose dust is there, take it; if not, put some there
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא puts both teachings together. If loose dust is on the floor, bring it. If none is there, place dust there and then take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If there is some there, bring it. If there is none there, put some there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by showing how both parts of the פסוק work together in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On the floor of the משכן' requires the dust to be taken from the floor. 'That is' requires it to be loose and not dug out. So if there is no loose dust, you place dust on the floor first, and then take it from there.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do both teachings fit together?

steps.whatToRemember: The dust for the סוטה's water must be taken from the floor of the היכל and must be loose. You may not bring it in from outside and use it directly, and you may not dig it out. If none is there, you put dust on the floor first and then take it.
steps.confusionAlert: Putting dust there from elsewhere does not contradict the first teaching. The dust is still taken from the floor of the משכן, because it was placed there first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source in the פסוק for the משנה's marble tile with loose dust underneath it.

phrases.english: How so?
If there is some there, bring it;
if there is none there, put some there.
phrases.notes: You place loose dust on the floor first and then pick it up from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the answers of Steps 25 and 27 into one practical rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Take loose dust from the floor of the היכל. If none is there, place dust there first and then take it.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: dust may be prepared outside and brought in
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from 'and of the dust that is' that the כהן would prepare dust outside and bring it into the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: 'And of the dust that is' teaches that the כהן would prepare dust outside and bring it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with its own reading of the same words in the פסוק. This ברייתא says the כהן could get the dust ready outside and then carry it inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא (Steps 24-28) used the words 'on the floor of the משכן' to show the dust must come from inside. This ברייתא focuses on 'the dust that is' (literally 'that will be') and reads it to allow dust brought in from outside. That is close to the first ברייתא's fallback case, where dust is placed on the floor when there is none there.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the first ברייתא. It started with the idea of preparing dust outside and rejected it. This ברייתא actually teaches that idea from the פסוק.

phrases.english: It was taught in another [ברייתא]:
"And of the dust that is, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:17

phrases.english: teaches that he would prepare [dust]
from outside and bring it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that reads the same פסוק differently from the one in Steps 24-28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'the dust that is', the כהן may prepare dust outside and bring it into the משכן.

steps.title: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה begins explaining 'on the floor of the משכן'
steps.stepSummary: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה says the words 'on the floor of the משכן' come to include another floor. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On the floor of the משכן': אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה says this comes to include the floor of...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next words of the פסוק and begins quoting אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה. This step sets up his teaching, which finishes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'To include' means the words widen the rule beyond the simple case of the משכן in the desert. Which floor is included only becomes clear when the sentence continues.

phrases.english: "On the floor of the Tabernacle":
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:17

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda says:
to include the floor of

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְהָבִיא קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by explaining the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'on the floor of the משכן' come to include another floor beyond the משכן itself. The details continue in the next lines.
